tier_reason: First-party: README states the CPU (Intel Core i7-10850H, single thread) and the repo has the benchmark code (benchs/bench_all.cpp, which times Blosc2 shuffle/bitshuffle with zstd and lz4), but no compiler or flags are given and results appear only as ratio-vs-speed curves in docs/benchmarks.svg with no numeric table.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README: Stenos 'usually compress better and faster than Blosc + Zstd or lz4'; the SIMD block algorithm 'can compress at more or less 2GB/s and decompress at 3GB/s'. docs/benchmarks.svg plots ratio against speed for 10 files from stenos_dataset (e.g. 16_2048_sq_float4.bin, 2_WA.txt, 8_SHYBPTOT.txt) comparing Stenos only with Zstd+Byteshuffle and Zstd+bitshuffle; no LZ4 curve and no numeric values in text.
corrections.baseline: Blosc2 byte shuffle + Zstd and Blosc2 bitshuffle + Zstd
corrections.caveats: Own benchmark and dataset; compiler and flags not stated; numbers only as SVG curves. The README's 'or lz4' claim is not shown in the published graph, although benchs/bench_all.cpp contains Blosc2+LZ4 variants. Baseline is Blosc+Zstd, not plain zstd; specialised for typed binary arrays, not a general byte compressor. Stenos depends on Zstd and borrows Blosc's shuffle code and a simplified LZ4.

notes: Metadata OK: MIT, 18 stars, last commit 2026-09-21, not a fork. SVG text labels were parsed; plotted values were not extracted.
